title: Gluing the local tower adjunctions
statement:
In the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], fix a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite type, of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Use the ordinary derived category of the strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and its uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], with $Rf_{!,\bullet}$ and its finite evaluations as in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Tate twists are taken levelwise as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

For each $K_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ there is a pair $(G_\bullet,\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet))$, with $G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet K_\bullet\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ and $\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet):Rf_{!,\bullet}G_\bullet\to K_\bullet$, such that
$$a\longmapsto\varepsilon_\bullet(K_\bullet)\circ Rf_{!,\bullet}(a):\operatorname{Hom}(M_\bullet,G_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\bullet}M_\bullet,K_\bullet)$$
is a bijection for every $M_\bullet$ in that category, natural in $M_\bullet$, and:

1. On every coordinate chart $f|_U=p_d\circ e$, $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ etale, there is a counit-preserving isomorphism $G_\bullet|_U\simeq e_\bullet^*p_{d,\bullet}^*K_\bullet(d)[2d]$. The local counit applies the fibre sum for $e$ followed by iterated projective-line integration.
2. The pair is unique up to unique counit-preserving isomorphism, and $K_\bullet\mapsto f^!_\bullet K_\bullet$ is a functor right adjoint to $Rf_{!,\bullet}$.
3. There are natural isomorphisms $(f^!_\bullet K_\bullet)_n\simeq f^!_{A_n}K_n$, compatible with counits and units. Under them the reduction map from level $n$ to $m\leq n$ is
$$ (f^!_{A_n}K_n)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\xrightarrow{c_{n,m}(K_n)}f^!_{A_m}(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m)\xrightarrow{f^!_{A_m}(r^K_{n,m})}f^!_{A_m}K_m,$$
where $c_{n,m}$ is the coefficient comparison of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional].

source.place: node det-sp-tower-gluing, order None

proof.text: Fix $K=K_\bullet$ and abbreviate $F_Z=R(f|_Z)_{!,\bullet}$ for opens $Z\subseteq X$. The standing schemes are Noetherian: a field has just the ideals $0,(1)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies to the structure morphisms. The statement [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] then says that $X$ and every open in it are Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-sc-standard-smooth-local-relative-dimension] every point has a standard-smooth affine neighbourhood of relative dimension $d$ over an affine open $T\subseteq Y$. The etale polynomial chart of [lem-sc-standard-smooth-etale-polynomial-chart] gives $U\to\mathbf A^d_T$; composing with $\mathbf A^d_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y$ remains etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Thus choose a finite cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^rU_i$ by such charts. Every open subset of a chart is again a chart by the same etale composition statement. If $X$ is empty, the zero pair represents the zero functor; henceforth use induction on $r\geq1$.

source.place: Local pairs and Gluing: existence of a finite coordinate cover

proof.text: The finite levels in [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers] are already the ordinary derived categories over the constant rings $A_n$, with intrinsic constructibility and Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. No condensed or completed category comparison is needed. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], writing $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ gives $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$, a finite commutative ring. A finite ring is Noetherian since its set of ideals is finite. All schemes under consideration, including opens and intermediate affine/projective spaces, are separated finite-type $k$-schemes; Step 1's argument makes them Noetherian and qcqs. Hence the equivalence in [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] supplies an etale-origin witness for each ctf level, preserving its specified Tor interval. These witnesses are chosen separately at each level, with no assertion that they form a tower. Uniform cohomological vanishing makes the tower bounded below: cohomology in the Grothendieck tower category is levelwise by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian].

source.place: Uniformity: local right-adjoint and compact-support bounds

proof.text: Check the proposed local object $H_UK=e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d]$ belongs to the tower category. By [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels], inverse image on towers is exact and computed levelwise. It preserves intrinsic constructibility [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: pull back a finite locally closed stratification and each constant finite-module local model; on our Noetherian schemes these pulled-back locally closed strata are constructible. For Tor amplitude $[u,v]$, [lem-sf-flat-model] gives a flat model supported in that precise interval, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] says its inverse-image terms remain flat. Exact inverse image preserves the quasi-isomorphism, so the interval is unchanged. Here the flat-model coefficient is the uniformizer quotient of exponent $en$, exactly our $A_n$. The finite twist is locally free of rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], so tensoring with it preserves these conditions. Thus if $K_n$ has cohomological support $[a,b]$ and Tor interval $[u,v]$, $H_UK_n$ has the intervals $[a-2d,b-2d]$ and $[u-2d,v-2d]$, independently of $n$. These are precisely the membership requirements of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. The same reasoning applies to each intermediate inverse image and twist.

source.place: Uniformity: local right-adjoint and compact-support bounds

proof.text: Every open restriction $f|_Z$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Its fibres are open in the pure-$d$ smooth fibres of $f$, so every nonempty fibre still has pure dimension $d$. The geometric-point base changes preserve that relative dimension by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1). Thus [sk-lem-sp-tower-bound] makes $F_Z=R(f|_Z)_{!,\bullet}$ a functor between the uniform ctf tower categories. More explicitly [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform], with finite ordinary rings $A_n$ and the etale-origin witnesses of Step 2, gives Tor interval $[u,v+2d]$ and cohomology vanishing outside the same interval whenever the input levels have common Tor interval $[u,v]$. This verifies the required compact-support preservation hypotheses at every open and intermediate projection used below.

source.place: Uniformity: local right-adjoint and compact-support bounds

proof.text:
Let $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$ and $p=qj$, for each intermediate base $S$. Here $\ell$ is invertible, and Step 2 supplies bounded-below etale-origin domains for every ctf tower used. The extension $j_!M$ is again ctf by [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](2). Consequently the actual $\mathscr C^+$ domains and the ctf restriction of [det-sp-tower-p1-adjunction] apply, with no need for compatible etale witnesses. Its adjunction and the open adjunction of the calculus give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_{!,\bullet}M,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(Rq_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}M,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_{!,\bullet}M,q^*_\bullet K(1)[2])\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,p^*_\bullet K(1)[2]).$$
The functor identification is the compactification composition/open normalization of the calculus. The adjunction maps are actual tower morphisms and evaluate to the finite maps, by both cited statements.

source.place: Local pairs: affine line, iteration, etale composition

proof.text: The finite twist identification [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level] applies with uniformizer exponent $en$ and $N=n$. Pullback of a root of unity commutes with $u\mapsto u^\ell$, since pullback preserves multiplication; after extending scalars these finite identifications therefore give compatible maps of twist towers. Use the monoidal derived pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] on the ringed inverse-system topoi and the tensor-power definition [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Tensor associators then identify successive pulled-back twists with their sum twist as an actual tower isomorphism, before evaluating. Compose the Hom bijections of Step 5 for the $d$ affine-line projections and then with the etale adjunction $e_!\dashv e^*$ of [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus]. This gives the chart pair $(H_UK,\varepsilon_U)$ with $H_UK=e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d]$. For $d=0$ use the identity projection adjunction. The composite counit is $\varepsilon_{p_d}\circ Rp_{d!}(\varepsilon_e)$: fibre summation precedes integration. All its finite evaluations have the specified finite counits and units. Conservativity is used only to test invertibility of constructed comparisons, never to infer equality of derived tower morphisms.

source.place: Local pairs: affine line, iteration, etale composition

proof.text:
Suppose $U,V$ cover an open $Z\subseteq X$, with pairs $(G_U,\varepsilon_U)$ and $(G_V,\varepsilon_V)$ already representing the local functors; put $W=U\cap V$. For an open inclusion $i:W\hookrightarrow U$, [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] gives $F_W=F_Ui_!$ and $i_!\dashv i^*$, with $i_!$ preserving the constructible tower category. Thus
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_U|_W)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(i_!N,G_U)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_WN,K).$$
The associated counit is $\varepsilon_U\circ F_U(i_!i^*G_U\to G_U)$. With $i_V:W\hookrightarrow V$ the second restriction has the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_V|_W)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(i_{V!}N,G_V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_WN,K)$ and counit $\varepsilon_V\circ F_V(i_{V!}i_V^*G_V\to G_V)$. There is a unique counit-preserving isomorphism $c:G_U|_W\to G_V|_W$: apply the second representing bijection to the first counit to get $c$, and reverse the roles to get its inverse; injectivity of the two bijections makes both composites identities. This argument uses representing pairs on $W$, rather than asserting that arbitrary local derived isomorphisms glue uniquely.

source.place: Gluing: the canonical overlap identification

proof.text:
By [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], the coefficient towers on $Z$ are modules over the ring object $\mathcal O_{E,Z}/\ell^\bullet$ in the Grothendieck topos of inverse systems of pro-etale sheaves. The constant inverse systems of the subterminal sheaves $U,V,W$ are open subtopoi with $U\cup V=Z$. For each open $D=U,V,W$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1) identifies $D_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}/D$, and (2) identifies the restricted constant ring $A_n$ with its constant ring on $D$. These identifications preserve the constant-section quotient maps $A_n\to A_m$. Applying them levelwise identifies the slice module category with the coefficient-tower category on $D$: its objects and arrows are the restricted module sheaves and semilinear transitions. Apply [lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent](1) in this ringed topos to $G_U,G_V,c$. It gives an actual object $G\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(Z,\mathcal O_E))$ with the prescribed restrictions. Concretely it is the fibre, not the unshifted cone, of
$$Rj_{U*}G_U\oplus Rj_{V*}G_V\longrightarrow Rj_{W*}(G_V|_W).$$
The intermediate derived direct images need not be constructible; the glued object is. Exact restriction and evaluation show its cohomology vanishes outside the common local interval. Each cohomology sheaf is intrinsically constructible by [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: combine the finitely many local stratifications, refining their finitely many intersections and complements to a finite locally closed stratification of the Noetherian scheme. The same restriction test applied to $G_n\otimes^L N$ gives its common Tor interval. A sheaf vanishing on both members is zero by the sheaf condition. Consequently $G$ belongs to the category of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers].

source.place: Gluing and Uniformity: construct the global object correctly

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent](2) to $G$ and then the exact compact-support functor $F_Z$ of [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus]. The result is the triangle
$$F_W(G|_W)\to F_U(G|_U)\oplus F_V(G|_V)\to F_ZG\longrightarrow.$$
Under the selected restriction isomorphisms, the map $(\varepsilon_U,\varepsilon_V)$ to $K$ kills the first arrow: its two components are the same overlap counit by the definition of $c$ in Step 7, and the first arrow has signs $(1,-1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact](i) it factors through a map $\varepsilon:F_ZG\to K$. This is the needed global counit. Only existence of this lift has been used.

source.place: Gluing: lift the compatible local counits

proof.text: For arbitrary $M$ in the constructible tower category, apply the two contravariant functors $\operatorname{Hom}(-,G)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(F_Z(-),K)$ to the open-cover triangle of Step 9 with $M$ in place of $G$. The arrows $\theta_N:a\mapsto\varepsilon F_Z(a)$ form a morphism of these exact Hom sequences: for each triangle arrow $t:N\to N'$ one has $\varepsilon F_Z(a\circ t)=\varepsilon F_Z(a)\circ F_Z(t)$, including the shifted boundary arrow. Exactness at all positions follows by rotations and shifts from [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact]. By [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] and the local adjunctions, $\theta$ is a bijection on all shifts of $j_{U!}(M|_U)$, $j_{V!}(M|_V)$ and $j_{W!}(M|_W)$. Indeed transposing $a:j_{U!}N\to G$ gives $a_U:N\to G_U$, and $\theta(a)=\varepsilon_UF_U(a_U)$ by the restriction equation of Step 9. For $D=U,V,W$, let $j_D:D\hookrightarrow Z$ and let $\varepsilon_D$ be the restricted representing counit. For every integer $t$, the open adjunction sends $a:j_{D!}(N[t])\to G$ to $a_D:N[t]\to G|_D$, and the restriction equation gives $\theta(a)=\varepsilon_DF_D(a_D)$. Thus each shifted vertical map is exactly the corresponding local representing bijection. In the five-term segment of the two exact sequences with $\theta_M$ in the centre, the other four vertical arrows are bijective. To see the central bijectivity directly, lift the image of a bottom central element to the top term on its right; its next image is zero by the rightmost injection, so exactness lifts it to the top centre, and the residual bottom element comes from the left and can be lifted using the left surjection. For injectivity a central kernel element has zero right image, hence comes from the top left; its bottom left image lies in the image of the preceding bottom term, which lifts by the leftmost surjection, leaving zero by the adjacent left injection. Thus $\theta_M$ is a bijection, natural in $M$. This proves representability of $(G,\varepsilon)$.

source.place: Gluing: the complete Hom-sequence argument

proof.text: Use induction on the finite cover in Step 1. For a single chart the pair is Step 6. Given the pair on $Z=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_{r-1}$, use $U=Z$, $V=U_r$ in Steps 7–10. The intersection is an open of the chart $U_r$, so its chart pair is available, and Step 7 also identifies the restriction of the pair from $Z$ with it. This constructs the pair on $X$. For an additional coordinate chart $j:D\hookrightarrow X$, the open adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ and the open normalization $F_Xj_!=F_D$ of [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](1),(2) give $\operatorname{Hom}(N,G|_D)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N,G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_DN,K)$, with counit $\varepsilon F_X(j_!j^*G\to G)$. The unique counit-preserving comparison of representing pairs therefore identifies $G|_D$ with the chart pair in Step 6. This proves clause 1 for every chart, not just the chosen atlas.

source.place: Gluing: finite induction and arbitrary charts

proof.text: If $(G,\varepsilon)$ and $(G',\varepsilon')$ represent the same functor, take $M=G$ in the second bijection to obtain the unique $a:G\to G'$ with $\varepsilon'F(a)=\varepsilon$. Reversing the roles gives $b:G'\to G$; injectivity gives $ba=1$ and $ab=1$. For $u:K\to L$, define $G(u)$ as the unique map with $\varepsilon_LF(G(u))=u\varepsilon_K$. Applying this equation twice proves preservation of identities and composition. It also proves naturality in $K$ of the representing bijections. Set $\eta_M$ equal to the transpose of $1_{FM}$. The transpose equations give $\varepsilon_{FM}F(\eta_M)=1_{FM}$ and, by injectivity, $G(\varepsilon_K)\eta_{GK}=1_{GK}$. These are the two adjunction identities and prove clause 2 without requiring a functorial choice of cones.

source.place: Uniqueness and functoriality: explicit inverse maps and adjunction

proof.text: Evaluation at $n$ is exact by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], so it descends to a triangulated functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The input towers here are bounded below by their uniform bounds. Thus [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](1) identifies the evaluated compact-support functor with the finite operation for the same chosen compactification. The open extension and its evaluated adjunction maps are those of [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](2). By [det-sp-tower-p1-adjunction] and the compositions in Steps 5–6, evaluated chart counits and units are the finite ones. Only the unrestricted evaluation clause of det-sp-tower-shriek-levels is used; its projection formula with the extra algebraically closed finite-field hypothesis is not invoked.

source.place: Levels: finite representability and units, without exchanging evaluation and Hom

proof.text: Prove finite representability by induction on the same chart cover as Step 11. The empty case is the zero category. For a single chart the finite chart adjunction is obtained by the same composed Hom bijections as Steps 5–6. All finite ctf test objects and their open extensions admit etale-origin witnesses by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] on our qcqs schemes over finite Noetherian $A_n$; hence the stated finite projective-line domains apply, not merely objects that lift to a tower. For the induction step write $Z=U\cup V$, $W=U\cap V$, and evaluate the constructed pair to $(G_{Z,n},\varepsilon_{Z,n})$. Its restrictions have the finite representing counits by the induction hypothesis, the finite chart case on $V,W$, and the evaluated restriction equation of Step 9. For arbitrary finite ctf $M$ on $Z$, [lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent](2) gives the triangle $A\to B\to M\to A[1]$, with $A=j_{W!}(M|_W)$ and $B=j_{U!}(M|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(M|_V)$. These terms stay ctf by [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](2). No lift of $M$ to a tower is assumed.

source.place: Levels: finite representability and units, without exchanging evaluation and Hom

proof.text:
The rotations and shifts of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] give the exact segment
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B[1],G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,G_{Z,n})\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,G_{Z,n})$$
and the segment with terms $\operatorname{Hom}(F_{Z,n}(-),K_n)$. The vertical maps are $a\mapsto\varepsilon_{Z,n}F_{Z,n}(a)$. For every triangle arrow $t$, including its shifted boundary, $\varepsilon_{Z,n}F_{Z,n}(a\circ t)=\varepsilon_{Z,n}F_{Z,n}(a)F_{Z,n}(t)$, proving commutativity. The open adjunctions of [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] and the evaluated restriction equation identify the four outer vertical maps with local representing bijections on the appropriate shifts. The central map is bijective by the explicit five-term chase of Step 10: lift the right image, use exactness to lift centrally, and lift the residual from the left; for a kernel element lift from the left and subtract the lift from the preceding term. This proves finite representability for all $M$ and completes induction.

source.place: Levels: finite representability and units, without exchanging evaluation and Hom

proof.text: The constructible adjunction in [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] is on the ordinary constant-ring finite-Tor categories in our standing scheme setting and for the same coefficient-independent compactification. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is smooth of pure dimension $d\geq0$ and $A_n$ is finite and annihilated by $\ell^n$. Its finite representing pair therefore has a unique counit-preserving comparison $G_n\simeq f^!_{A_n}K_n$, by the elementary uniqueness argument of Step 12. Evaluating $\varepsilon_LF(G(u))=u\varepsilon_K$ identifies the action on each tower morphism with that of the finite adjoint. Evaluating $\varepsilon_{FM}F(\eta_M)=1$ gives the finite transpose equation for $1_{F_nM_n}$. Injectivity of the finite bijection identifies the units as well. This proves the level, counit and unit assertions of clause 3.

source.place: Levels: finite representability and units, without exchanging evaluation and Hom

proof.text:
Use the chosen compactification $f=\bar f j$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], the same one used in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](1). Apply [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] with $A=A_n$, $B=A_m$, $M=G_n$, and this compactification. The rings are finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]: $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$, $A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{em}$, for $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$. Since $1\leq m\leq n$ the quotient map is unital and both rings are killed by $\ell^n$. The object $G_n$ is in the ordinary ctf category by Steps 3, 8 and 16, and $f$ is separated finite type. Hence the canonical comparison is an isomorphism
$$b_f(G_n):(R\bar f_*j_!G_n)\otimes^L_{A_{n,Y}}A_{m,Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar f_*j_!(G_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,X}}A_{m,X}).$$
Its proper part is the $A_m$-linear adjoint transpose of the $A_n$-counit after extension of scalars, followed by the canonical open-extension tensor comparison, exactly the normalization of the cited statement. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $A_m$ over $A_n$ is required.

source.place: Levels: global counit-transpose calculation for reduction maps

proof.text:
Write $r_G:(G_n)_{A_m}\to G_m$ and $r_K:(K_n)_{A_m}\to K_m$ for the natural reduction maps of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. The counit-preserving comparisons from Step 16 are fixed throughout. The comparison $b_f(G_n)$ just specified is the one in [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](3); therefore $r^{FG}_{n,m}=F_{f,m}(r_G)b_f(G_n)$. Naturality of the reduction map for the actual tower counit $\varepsilon:FG\to K$ gives
$$\varepsilon_mF_{f,m}(r_G)b_f(G_n)=r_K(\varepsilon_n)_{A_m},$$
and hence
$$\varepsilon_mF_{f,m}(r_G)=r_K(\varepsilon_n)_{A_m}b_f(G_n)^{-1}.$$
Both sides have source $F_{f,m}((G_n)_{A_m})$ and target $K_m$. The inverse exists by Step 17. This equality is in the global derived category, not an inference from equalities on chart restrictions.

source.place: Levels: global counit-transpose calculation for reduction maps

proof.text:
For [det-sp-reduction-exceptional], the unital coefficient quotient $A_n\to A_m$ has common annihilator $N=\ell^n$ and uses the same coefficient-independent compactification and ordinary ctf categories as above. The finite identifications from Step 16 preserve precisely its counits. Apply its defining transpose equation to $K_n$ and use naturality of the finite counit:
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_mF_{f,m}\bigl(f^!_{A_m}(r_K)c_{n,m}(K_n)\bigr)
&=r_K\varepsilon_{m,(K_n)_{A_m}}F_{f,m}(c_{n,m}(K_n))\\
&=r_K(\varepsilon_n)_{A_m}b_f(G_n)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
These are the same source and target as in Step 18. Scalar extension preserves ctf here by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], so the finite adjunction may be tested on $(G_n)_{A_m}$. Injectivity of its Hom bijection gives $r_G=f^!_{A_m}(r_K)c_{n,m}(K_n)$, the required reduction formula without any normalization assumption. For $n=m$ the quotient reductions and comparisons are identities. For $n\geq m\geq r$, the composition clause of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] and the reduction composition law of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] identify both iterated transposes with the transpose for $A_n\to A_r$.

source.place: Levels: global counit-transpose calculation for reduction maps
